question: to the Commission Bruno Tobback (S&D) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on packaging and packaging waste (PPWR) establishes a common European framework for packaging and extended producer responsibility. However, producers must first register and comply with extended producer responsibility obligations separately in each Member State where they make packaging or packaged products available. Micro-enterprises selling to consumers across the EU may therefore have to navigate up to 27 national systems with different procedures, reporting requirements, contributions and authorised-representative costs. This multiplication can make entering another national market, or shipping to the EU, economically unviable, especially for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and micro-enterprises. This hinders businesses’ ability to scale across borders and fragments the single market. 1.

Has the Commission assessed whether cumulative national registration, reporting and payment obligations constitute a disproportionate barrier to cross-border trade for companies, particularly SMEs and micro-enterprises?

Will the Commission propose an EU one-stop shop providing a single channel for registration, harmonised reporting and payments for extended producer responsibility contributions? If so, will the Commission organise or oversee its governance and functioning? If not, does it envisage another means of harmonisation and cross-border recognition of registrations across Member States?
What measures will the Commission take, and when, to prevent national implementation of the PPWR from creating (further) barriers within the single market, in line with the single market strategy?
